question.worked_solution:
First, we need to find the equation of the parabola. From the diagram, we see that the parabola has a vertex at $(3,-1)$ and passes through the point $(0,\frac{5}{4}).$

The general standard equation of an up- or down-opening parabola with vertex $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
(x-h)^{2}=4p(y-k).
$$

Substituting $(h,k)=(3,-1)$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-3)^{2} & =4p(y+1).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to find $p.$ Since the parabola passes through the point $(0,\frac{5}{4}),$ we substitute $x=0$ and $y=\frac{5}{4}$ into the equation and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(0-3)^{2} & =4p(\frac{5}{4}+1) \\ 9 & =4p(\frac{9}{4}) \\ p & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the parabola is

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-3)^{2} & =4(y+1).\end{aligned}
$$

When the parabola intersects the $x$-axis, we must have $y=0.$ So, we substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the parabola and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-3)^{2} & =4(0+1) \\ (x-3)^{2} & =4 \\ x-3 & =\pm \sqrt{4} \\ x & =\pm 2+3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, from left to right, the $x$-intercepts are $1$  and $5.$
